repairedFor: voice.avoid.2: "best-seller" is social proof. Proof beats use facts the seller supplies, never invented ones.

audience.description: Adults who cook at home most nights and reach for hot sauce on eggs, tacos, noodles, pizza and leftovers. They like trying small-batch pantry items, care about flavor over pure heat, and enjoy food videos and cooking shows. They will pay a bit more for a bottle that tastes layered and looks good on the counter.

brief.productRole: The bottle is used across a fast sequence of everyday meals: a shake over fried eggs, a drizzle over a bowl of noodles, a dot on a taco, a swirl into a pan of roasted vegetables. A macro shot shows the sauce pouring slowly, thick and deep red, with flecks of chile and garlic. A final shot has an adult taking a bite, pausing, then reaching for the bottle again as the heat builds.

music.style: Upbeat funk-leaning indie groove with a tight drum break, muted electric guitar, warm bass and light hand percussion, a little retro, with a small snare fill on the final bite

visual.look: Warm natural-light kitchen look with rich reds and deep shadows, slight film grain, handheld 35mm-style framing with tight macro inserts on the pour and the food. Quick cuts of about one second each, a match cut on every shake of the bottle, and a slow-motion pour at the 10 second mark. The bottle label with the flame symbol stays visible and unobstructed in at least four shots. No readable text appears on screen except a simple end card.

wardrobe.styling: Casual home-cook looks: rolled-sleeve linen shirts, plain cotton tees, an apron in washed canvas, a dish towel over the shoulder. Earth tones and neutral colors, no logos or printed text on any clothing.

types: lived-in home kitchen with a wooden counter
small dining table by a window
stovetop with a cast iron pan

voice.tone: Dry, friendly and confident, like a cook who knows what is good and does not oversell it
use: Talk about flavor first: garlic, fruit sweetness, slow-building heat
Name specific foods the sauce goes on
Invite people to put it on everything
End with a simple call to shop the bottle
avoid: Ratings, reviews, popularity or sales claims of any kind
Speaking as a customer who tried it

hooks: Heat that waits a second before it shows up.
Your eggs called. They want garlic and chile.
Fermented, fruity, and it builds slowly.

talent.description: Three fictional adult home cooks in their late 20s to late 30s with different styles and energy: one relaxed adult cooking breakfast in the morning light, one animated adult plating noodles, and one calm adult at the table taking a bite and smiling as the heat builds. Natural, unposed, shown mostly from the shoulders down and in profile during meals, with close, genuine reactions.
